Stated Claim / Post Context:
Mobile bookstore pairs flowers with books at Nebraska markets

The Poppy Archive, owned by Emily Semm, operates out of a custom Japanese K-truck in Omaha and Lincoln

Actual Article Body:
LINCOLN, Neb. (KOLN) - A cat’s name, flowers and books added up to create a mobile bookstore called The Poppy Archive.

Owner Emily Semm named the business after her cat, Poppy, with poppy for the flower idea and archive for books.

“The whole thing is read more bloom more, so I attached flowers and their vibes to books that have the same vibe,” Semm said.

The Poppy Archive got its start this summer and has popped up in markets across Omaha and Lincoln.

“The fact that it’s mobile and on this K-truck which is actually from Japan, and I had it custom made with all of the bookshelves and things,” Semm said.

The Poppy Archive sells books and bridges the gap between readers and writers.

Cory Clark, who is an author, said it is not often he sees books at events like Haymarket Harvest.

“I have one published novel it’s called John the Cynic and it’s about a man losing his faith and a collection of short stories called Cosmic Soup,” Clark said.

Clark said the The Poppy Archive was the perfect pairing for a fall event like Haymarket Harvest.

“I love events like this that bring the community together, like we had never heard of the Poppy Archive and so it’s great to find stuff like this and make a connection with the owner,” Clark said.

For Semm, The Poppy Archive means more than an opportunity to sell books.

“I’ve always wanted to own a bookstore that’s always been my dream,” Semm said.

Semm will keep driving her dream forward in markets to come.
